To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a novel design of a network device that enables the selection of a PDSN for a mobile user based on the user's subscribed services and we implement the device on Linux.

we have designed and implemented a device called radio-packet redirection (RPSR), that works within the existing standards and allows the selection of the "best" packet data serving node based on a user identity.
RPSR is able to select the best PDSN for a user based on the user's identity and that the overhead of RPSR is very small.
In summary, our research is concerned with
enabling the network to support user-based services in CDMA200 network.
the design and implementation issues of a network entity that provides user identity based session redirection.
the following questions: 1) Can a device-independent session redirector be designed and implemented in a CDMA200O network?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RPSR enables user-based session redirection and thus provides a mechanism for a mobile node to access services based on user identity and not on the device identity.
the RPSR is an efficient and effective solution to the problem of session redirection in CDNA2000 networks.
we present a design and prototype implementation of an entity that enables a CDMA200 network to provide a number of useful services that were hitherto unavailable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RPSR is an effective and efficient solution for enabling user identity based service selection for CDMA2000 packet data networks.
RPSR is a device that sits between the radio network and the packet data network and enables user identity based session redirection.

RPSR provides the ability to decouple user services from device identity, and enables the use of user identity for PDSN selection, which in turn enables a number of new services in a CDMA200O network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current design of PCF is not optimal for the packet data services that are offered to the MNs and that the RPSR is a practical solution for the problem.
the current standard can be extended to enable new services without changing the existing infrastructure.
a device-independent user identity based session redirection mechanism can be implemented in a CDMA200 network using standard protocols.
